rounds.text: Annu Projects Ltd is trading near the bottom of its 52-week range at just 21% of that range [E4], yet the fundamental operating performance demonstrates elite capital efficiency with an ROCE of 27.25% against a sector benchmark of 11.76% [E9] and an ROE of 21.65% against a sector benchmark of 9.37% [E8]. This strong profitability is underpinned by consistent growth, highlighted by a 3-year compounded sales growth of 17% [E13] and an explosive 3-year compounded profit growth of 81% [E15], alongside an operating margin expansion of 9 percentage points to 18% in Mar 2025 [E19]. Furthermore, intrinsic value modelling via a discounted cash flow indicates a substantial margin of safety of 46.7% [E34], with a reverse DCF showing that the current market price only prices in a modest 9.3% earnings growth compared to the 18.0% base case [E35]. The company maintains a conservatively financed balance sheet with a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.20x [E25] and strong backing from promoters who hold 65.05% as of Sep 2026 [E29]. Conceded: operating cash flow was negative at Rs -35 Cr in Mar 2025 [E22] and the company has high debtors of 285 days [E38].

Annu Projects Ltd presents a severe disconnect between reported accounting profits and actual cash generation, highlighted by an operating cash flow of Rs -35 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -36 Cr in March 2025 [E22, E23]. This cash drain results in a deeply negative cash conversion ratio of -1.67x against reported profit, with operating cash flow plunging to -87% of operating profit [E21, E24]. Working capital risks are compounding rapidly, evidenced by exceptionally high debtors of 285 days and working capital days ballooning from 92.4 days to 170 days [E38, E39]. Furthermore, the company offers a dividend yield of 0.00%, returning nothing to shareholders despite its headline figures [E3], while borrowings have ticked upward to Rs 24 Cr in March 2025 [E27] and the yearly operating-margin trend remains inconsistent over the last two years [E20]. Conceded: [E8], [E9], [E13], [E15].

Conceded: [E22], [E23], [E27]. The cash drain and minor borrowing uptick are visible, but the bear ignores the company's conservative balance sheet where debt to equity remains low at 0.20x [E25]. While working capital days and debtors are elevated [E38, E39], the multi-year fundamentals demonstrate exceptional profitability that eclipses temporary cash timing issues, including a high ROCE of 27.25% against a sector benchmark of 11.76% and an ROE of 21.65% compared to the 9.37% sector benchmark [E8, E9]. Profit growth is robust with a 3-year compounded profit growth of 81% and an 18% growth over the trailing twelve months, outperforming the sector median profit growth of 12.6% [E15, E16, E47]. Operating margins have expanded by 9 percentage points over three years to reach 18% in March 2025 [E19]. Finally, the market price at 21% of its 52-week range [E4] heavily undervalues a company supported by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 135 per share, offering a substantial 46.7% margin of safety [E33, E34].

Conceded: [E8], [E9], [E15], [E16], [E19], [E33], [E34], [E47]. The bull's highlighted profitability metrics and DCF estimates do not erase the severe operational risks signalled by cash flow and working capital data [E21, E22, E23, E38, E39]. The reliance on a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.20x [E25] is contradicted by the reality that borrowings have climbed to Rs 24 Cr while operating cash flow plunged to a negative Rs -35 Cr and free cash flow dropped to Rs -36 Cr in March 2025 [E22, E23, E27]. Furthermore, the impressive reported profit and margin expansion [E15, E16, E19] are completely disconnected from actual cash generation, as evidenced by a cash conversion ratio of -1.67x and operating cash flow sitting at -87% of operating profit [E21, E24]. High debtors stretching to 285 days and working capital days surging from 92.4 to 170 days [E38, E39] explain why profits are failing to convert into real liquidity, rendering the margin of safety [E34] illusory. Finally, the stock trading at only 21% of its 52-week range [E4] is not a sign of undervaluation, but a rational market reflection of these severe working capital distress signals and inconsistent operating margins [E20].
